# Auth Guard Checklist: Account Creation (scope correctness)

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements around the `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` refusal are
written precisely enough to be built and reviewed without guesswork — specifically, that they say
exactly which accounts are refused, which are not, and when the refusal stops.
**Created**: 2026-09-01
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) — FR-015 to FR-018, FR-017a to FR-017c

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Which accounts are in scope

- [ ] CHK001 - Is the set of accounts subject to the refusal defined by a stored attribute rather
      than by inference from status or flag combinations? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017a-i]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are the three credential origins (`invite`, `admin_direct`, `admin_reset`)
      individually stated as in-scope or out-of-scope for the refusal, with none left implied?
      [Completeness, Spec §FR-017a, §FR-017a-ii]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is it explicit that carrying `mustChangePassword` is *not by itself* sufficient to
      trigger the refusal? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-017a-i]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is the exclusion of admin-reset accounts stated as a deliberate limitation with its
      reasoning, rather than left as an unexplained omission? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017a-ii]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are requirements defined for an account that is `admin_direct` but has *already*
      changed its password — i.e. is the post-change state unambiguously out of scope?
      [Coverage, Spec §FR-017b]
- [ ] CHK006 - Do the requirements state what governs an account whose origin is unknown or absent
      (e.g. a row predating the column), rather than leaving the default to the migration?
      [Gap, Spec §FR-017a-i]

## When the refusal stops

- [ ] CHK007 - Is "stops immediately, without re-login" stated as a requirement rather than left as
      an implementation consequence? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017a]
- [ ] CHK008 - Do the requirements specify that the decision is made from the account's current
      stored state rather than from a value captured at sign-in? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017a]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the relationship between clearing the flag and ending the refusal stated in one
      place, so the two cannot be implemented as independent conditions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017a,
      §FR-017b]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are requirements defined for a session that was issued *before* the password change,
      so it is clear whether an existing token continues to work? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK011 - Is the atomicity of "new password stored" and "flag cleared" specified, so a partial
      write cannot leave an account changed-but-still-refused? [Measurability, Spec §FR-017b]

## The exemption list

- [ ] CHK012 - Is the exempt set enumerated exactly, rather than described by a category such as
      "auth endpoints" or "read-only routes"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017a]
- [ ] CHK013 - Do the requirements state that anything not enumerated is refused, so the rule's
      default is closed rather than open? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017a]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is each exemption justified by what the user must be able to do (complete the change,
      or leave), so a future reader can judge whether a proposed addition belongs? [Clarity,
      Spec §FR-017a]
- [ ] CHK015 - Are read endpoints explicitly stated as non-exempt, given that a broad read exemption
      would be the most tempting relaxation? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-017a]

## Distinguishability by the client

- [ ] CHK016 - Is the refusal's machine-readable identifier specified exactly, and stated as the
      thing clients branch on? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017a]
- [ ] CHK017 - Do the requirements forbid distinguishing this refusal by message text, so wording
      can change without breaking a client? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017a]
- [ ] CHK018 - Are requirements defined for what the client does on receiving it, so the server
      contract and the frontend obligation are traceable to each other? [Traceability,
      Spec §FR-017a, §FR-017c]

## Interaction with existing rules

- [ ] CHK019 - Is the relationship between this refusal and FR-008's pending-account invariant
      stated, so the two rules cannot be read as conflicting? [Conflict, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are the requirements clear that direct creation produces no invite token, so no
      requirement elsewhere assumes every account has one? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK021 - Is it specified whether a directly-created account may later be sent an invite (e.g.
      via resend), or whether that is refused? [Coverage, Spec §US4/AC5]

## Notes

- Items are about whether the **requirements** are written unambiguously, not whether the guard
  behaves correctly — the latter belongs to tests in `tasks.md`.
- CHK006 and CHK010 are the two most likely to be genuinely unaddressed: both concern states the
  spec has not obviously considered (rows predating the column, and tokens issued before a change).
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state but does not modify these markers.
